executive_summary:
IHH demonstrates expansion beyond hyperinflation accounting: excluding MFRS129, revenue grew 7%, EBITDA 14% and PATMI excluding exceptional items 30%. Singapore admissions nevertheless fell 6%, while acquisitions, unresolved legal disclosures and funding obscure the risk-adjusted entry case. Maintain observation; the evidence does not yet establish a directional new-position advantage.

A positive MACD histogram and firmer RSI suggest a tentative rebound, but price remains below SMA-50 and SMA-200. Low volume and proximity to the 52-week low do not establish a durable trend reversal. IHH has a relatively defensive demand profile, but macro resilience does not itself establish medical volume or margin improvement. Cost and currency effects leave the macro signal neutral. bull_case: IHH shows adjusted operating growth beyond PATMI: revenue and EBITDA improved excluding MFRS129. Round two uses this as an independent operating counterweight to lower Singapore admissions, while keeping funding and legal clarity as explicit thesis gates. Strongest disconfirming evidence to caution: Revenue +7%, EBITDA +14% and PATMI excluding exceptional items +30% excluding MFRS129 provide strong growth after removing an important accounting distortion.
bear_case: Acquisitions complicate comparability, Singapore admissions fell and legal/governance statements remain unresolved. Round two accepts that growth is not merely an accounting headline but distinguishes EBITDA from shareholder cash after financing and unquantified legal exposure.
